Which formula shows the way in which atoms are bonded in a molecule but does not show all the bond lines?

A Empirical
B Molecular
C Structural
D Condensed structural
memo:
* $\checkmark\checkmark$ D (or Condensed structural)

**Reasoning:**
A condensed structural formula represents the arrangement of atoms in a molecule without showing all carbon-carbon and carbon-hydrogen bond lines (e.g. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$). A structural formula shows all the bonds and atoms, while empirical and molecular formulas show only atom ratios or totals without depicting bonding connections.

$$\text{Mg(s)} + 2\text{HC}\ell\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{MgC}\ell_2\text{(aq)} + \text{H}_2\text{(g)}$$
question:
Which ONE of the following changes will INCREASE the YIELD of $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$?

A Crush the piece of magnesium.
B Use a $3\text{ g}$ piece of magnesium.
C Use a greater volume of the acid.
D Use a higher concentration of the acid.
memo:
* $\checkmark\checkmark$ B (or Use a $3\text{ g}$ piece of magnesium.)

**Reasoning:**
Hydrochloric acid is present in EXCESS, making magnesium the limiting reactant. The yield (total amount of product formed) depends directly on the amount of the limiting reactant. Increasing the mass of magnesium from $2\text{ g}$ to $3\text{ g}$ increases the moles of limiting reactant, thereby increasing the maximum theoretical yield of $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$. Crushing magnesium, increasing acid concentration, or increasing acid volume can affect the reaction rate, but do not increase the maximum yield.

Curve Q is obtained after a change was made to one reaction condition:
- Curve P has a peak at a specific kinetic energy and height.

A Addition of a catalyst
B Increase in temperature
C Increase in activation energy
D Increase in the concentration of the reactants

* $\checkmark\checkmark$ D (or Increase in the concentration of the reactants)

**Reasoning:**
An increase in concentration increases the total number of reactant molecules per unit volume without altering their temperature (and thus without altering the average kinetic energy). A $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$
B $\text{HPO}_4^{2-}$
